# Appendix: An R Reference for the Researcher

## Tests Quick Reference

| Goal | Parametric | Non-parametric | Categorical |
|------|------------|----------------|-------------|
| Two indep. groups | `t.test(x, y)` | `wilcox.test(x, y)` | `chisq.test`, `fisher.test` |
| Two paired groups | `t.test(x, y, paired = TRUE)` | `wilcox.test(..., paired = TRUE)` | `mcnemar.test` |
| > 2 groups | `aov(y ~ g)` | `kruskal.test(y ~ g)` | `chisq.test` |
| Repeated measures | `lme4::lmer` | `friedman.test` | --- |
| Association (numeric) | `cor.test(x, y)` | `cor.test(..., method = "spearman")` | --- |
| Modeling | `lm`, `glm`, `lmer` | regression on ranks | logistic regression |

## Confidence Interval Quick Reference

```r
t.test(x)$conf.int
prop.test(k, n)$conf.int
wilcox.test(x, conf.int = TRUE)$conf.int
boot.ci(boot(x, stat, R = 5000), type = "bca")
```

## Reproducibility Snippet

```r
set.seed(20260525)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "sessionInfo.txt")
```

## Recommended Further Reading

- @wasserman2004all --- one-volume rigorous reference.
- @gelman2020regression --- modern applied perspective.
- @jain1991art --- the CS classic.
- @georges2007rigorous --- rigorous Java performance evaluation.
- @arcuri2014hitchhiker --- stats for randomized algorithms in SE.
- @wasserstein2016asa --- ASA statement on p-values.
- @wickham2017r4ds --- tidyverse entry point.

## A Closing Word

Statistics is a craft. The tests are tools, not rituals. Ask: what claim am I trying to support, and what evidence would convince a skeptical reader? Answer it with pre-registered designs, honest measurements, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and reproducible R scripts.
